data.outcome_summary: This PIRLS 2021 national report for Qatar presents descriptive results for Grade 4 reading achievement and related contextual factors. The study is based on PIRLS 2021’s international reading assessment administered to students at the end of Grade 4, with Qatar participating in the 2021 cycle (and previously in 2006 and every five years). The report states that Qatar’s sample comprised 5,253 students from 259 participating classes/schools, selected via a two-stage clustered sampling design (schools/classes, then one class randomly selected within the target grade). It reports achievement on the PIRLS scale (international mean set at 500) and proficiency levels (400, 475, 550, 625), including differences by gender, nationality (Qatari vs non-Qatari), and school type (government, Ministry-standard private, international, expatriate/community). It also discusses COVID-19 impacts on administration and compares paper vs digital modes for the transition stage, reporting very small differences, and provides contextual associations from questionnaires (home resources, early literacy activities, school climate, engagement, and attitudes toward reading).
